response: ## The finding `crime_00041` — **Oversized Raster** on `src/assets/hero-banner.png` > `byte size: 260,000 bytes (253.9 KB)` > `severity ladder: low ≥ 200 KB · medium ≥ 500 KB · high ≥ 1000 KB` > `format: png` Severity `low` (0.4), confidence `0.95`, effort `quick`, agent_risk `0.14`. ## Verdict: request changes, don't block 254 KB sits on the bottom rung of the ladder — it's 27% over the `low` threshold and less than half of `medium`. Nothing about it is unsafe, it can't break a build, and agent_risk is negligible (0.14, the second-lowest in the report). A hard block would be disproportionate to a low finding. But it should not merge as-is, for two reasons the detector can't see: 1. **A landing-page hero is almost always the LCP element.** 254 KB on the critical path is the single worst place in the repo to spend those bytes. The same file in `/docs` wouldn't be worth a comment. 2. **`effort: quick`.** The fix is one `sharp`/`cwebp` invocation and a `` tag. When the fix is cheaper than the discussion, take the fix. So: request changes, expect a re-push of the asset, approve on the follow-up. **One caveat on the evidence.** The finding gives bytes and format but *no dimensions* — compare `crime_00038`, which reports `32 × 32 px` for `check-icon.png`. Without intrinsic dimensions I can't tell you whether this is a 4000px master being downscaled by the browser or an appropriately-sized PNG that's simply the wrong codec. My sizing below assumes a conventional full-bleed hero; confirm against the actual layout before committing to the numbers. ## The transformation **Target dimensions.** For a full-bleed hero in a typical ~1280–1440px max-width layout, cap the largest raster at **1600px wide** (≈1600×900 at 16:9, or 1600×600 if it's a shorter band). Then ship a `srcset` rather than one file: ```html ``` Two things that matter as much as the bytes: set explicit `width`/`height` (or `aspect-ratio`) so the hero doesn't cause CLS, and set `fetchpriority="high"` with **no** `loading="lazy"` — lazy-loading the LCP element is a common own-goal. Don't ship a 3200px 2× variant. On a photographic hero, 1× at 1600px with slightly more aggressive quality beats 2× at conservative quality for the same byte budget; retina sharpness on a large soft photo is not where users notice. **Format: AVIF first, WebP fallback.** AVIF is the right primary for a photographic hero — it typically lands **30–50% smaller than WebP at equivalent perceived quality** on large photographic content, because it gets film grain and smooth gradients (sky, skin, bokeh) far cheaper than WebP's VP8-derived intra coding. Its weaknesses — slow encode, and poor handling of small images with hard edges — don't apply here: encode happens once at build time, and a hero is the largest, softest image on the page. That's AVIF's best case. Keep the WebP source as a fallback anyway. Support is no longer the reason (AVIF is fine in current Chrome, Firefox, and Safari 16+); the reason is that `` gives it to you for free and it covers older Safari and in-app webviews, which are over-represented in landing-page traffic from social links. **One exception:** if the hero is a flat illustration, a logo lockup, or contains rendered text with hard edges, invert this — lossy AVIF will ring on those edges. Use lossless WebP instead, which will typically beat the PNG by 25%+ with no artifacts at all. **Budget.** Set a hero budget of ~120 KB and enforce it. A 1600px photographic AVIF at roughly q50–60 usually lands 40–80 KB — a 3–5× reduction from the current 254 KB. The underlying mistake worth naming in the review comment: **PNG is a lossless format being used for photographic content.** That's the root cause, not the file size. The size is just the symptom the detector could measure. ## Adjacent, out of scope for this PR Two other asset findings in the same tree, if you want to batch the image-pipeline work: - `crime_00034` (**high**, 0.95) — `src/assets/partner-logo.svg` embeds two base64 rasters. Higher severity than the one you asked about. - `crime_00038` (low) — `src/assets/check-icon.png` is a 32×32 PNG that should be SVG. Neither belongs in this PR. Worth a follow-up ticket.
